text:
Maya (support): heads-up — multiple APAC customers reporting large latency spikes and auth failures since ~02:14 UTC. Seems traffic is getting routed to eu-west; customers see token validation errors.

Evan (eng-platform): I see healthcheck alerts — ap-sg synthetic probes flipped to DOWN at 02:14:12 which triggered automated failover to eu-west. Investigating cause.

InfraBot: [alert] synthetic-probe healthcheck ap-sg -> FAILED (504) 02:14:12

Priya (eng-sre): can you paste a probe log or sample curl output? Any DNS changes or infra deploys around that time?

Liam (support): customer repro: from their host in SG `curl -w "%{time_total}s" -o /dev/null -s https://api.redwood.example/v1/health` -> 0.82s and intermittent `{"error":"token_expired"}` even though token refresh succeeded locally. Ticket #INC-3209.

Tom (network): ran `dig +short api.redwood.example @1.1.1.1` from one probe host -> returned:
54.230.12.11
13.248.45.9
34.89.1.2
But `getent hosts api.redwood.example` on the probe shows only the eu-west IP and TTL ~18000. Authoritative TTL is 300. Looks like local resolver cache stale.

Nora (oncall): that mismatch would make probes target the wrong region; tokens minted for ap-sg would be rejected by eu-west endpoints -> auth errors. Could explain failover.

Evan (eng-platform): repro on a probe box: `curl -v https://api.redwood.example/health`
<- TLS SNI: eu-west.api.redwood.example
<- HTTP 502 from eu-west
Logs show `Received token: region=ap-sg; connection->region=eu-west` which triggers policy to reject.

Priya (eng-sre): quick triage steps I'm running:
1) enumerate probe resolvers: `pssh -i -h ap-sg-probes 'cat /etc/resolv.conf; systemd-resolve --status'`
2) check for nscd/chrony causing long-lived cache: `systemctl status nscd`
3) inspect local `/etc/hosts` and any startup scripts that pre-populate records.

Liam (support): telling affected customers: "We're investigating a regional routing discrepancy caused by stale probe DNS caches that momentarily redirected traffic. Engineers are applying mitigations now." :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Evan (eng-platform): immediate mitigation I'm proposing:
- force DNS cache flush on probe fleet (`sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches` + restart nscd where present)
- temporarily disable automated failover for 5m to avoid cascade from a few stale probes
- add a guard that failover requires >X failing probes AND majority of regional probes showing failure
I'll open rollout now.

DeployBot: rollback/disruption control: automated failover suppression requested by Evan at 02:22:05 UTC — in progress.

Tom (network): executed cache flush on 12 out of 14 ap-sg probes; after flush `dig +short api.redwood.example` returns expected ap endpoints and TTL 300. Healthchecks turning green.

Maya (support): verified with one customer — latency returned to normal, auth errors disappeared. Customer updated: "Thanks — looks fine now."

Priya (eng-sre): post-incident action items:
- update probe image to avoid long-lived DNS caches and ensure resolvers respect authoritative TTLs (owner: Priya)
- change failover logic to require majority/probe quorum instead of single-probe triggers (owner: Evan)
- add synthetic validation that checks token-region header against destination region to avoid silent routing mismatches (owner: Priya)
- add runbook steps for support to surface DNS-cache symptoms quickly (owner: Liam)

Evan (eng-platform): I'll add an alert: if failover triggers but >50% of probes for origin region remain healthy, suppress full failover and escalate to oncall instead.

Liam (support): will follow up with customers and close INC-3209 once postmortem links and ETA for fixes are ready. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

Priya (eng-sre): creating postmortem draft and linking runbook: https://confluence.internal/redwood/INC-3209-dns-probe-cache

Nora (oncall): marking incident as resolved for now; keeping monitoring window open for 2 hours.

Maya (support): closing the support thread after customer confirmation. Good catch everyone.
